properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 8 at 9:58AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 2.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Thursday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.0 feet
just after midnight tonight and linger at or just above Moderate
Flood Stage through this weekend.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 3.1
feet on 09/10/2005.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal; Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued October 8 at 8:19AM CDT until October 11 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 6
to 10 feet developing Friday morning in the surf zone builds to
12 to 18 feet over the Alabama beaches and 20 to 25 feet over
the northwest Florida beaches Friday night. These heights likely
to linger through Saturday. Surf begins to abate Saturday night
but remains high through Sunday morning.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday
night. For the High Surf Warning, from 7 AM Friday to 10 AM
CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening swimming
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE SATURDAY NIGHT... ...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 7 AM FRIDAY TO 10 AM CDT SUNDAY

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 8 at 6:15AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
Areas of fog, some locally dense, have developed early this
morning in the lowland of Lane County in the southern Willamette
Valley, resulting in roadway visibility of one mile or less.
Morning commuters should expect to encounter areas of rapidly
changing visibility.

If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you. If walking or cycling, wear bright or
reflective clothing and carry a light to increase your visibility
to drivers.

properties.areaDesc: East Entrance U.S. Waters Strait Of Juan De Fuca
properties.headline: Gale Watch issued October 8 at 5:30AM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, dense fog will reduce
visibility to 1 NM or less. For the Small Craft Advisory, west
winds 20 to 30 kt. For the Gale Watch, west winds 20 to 30 kt,
with gusts up to 40 kt possible.

* WHERE...East Entrance U. S. Waters Strait Of Juan De Fuca.

* WHEN...For the Dense Fog Advisory, until 10 AM PDT this
morning. For the Small Craft Advisory, from 2 PM this
afternoon to 3 AM PDT Friday. For the Gale Watch, from late
tonight through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility. Low visibility
will make navigation difficult.
properties.instruction:
A Gale Watch is issued when the risk of gale force winds of 34 to
47 knots has significantly increased, but the specific timing
and/or location is still uncertain. It is intended to provide
additional lead time for mariners who may wish to consider
altering their plans.

If you must navigate, proceed with caution. Use proper fog
signals. Make sure all running lights are on. Remember to use
your radar and compass.

NWSheadline: DENSE FOG ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM PDT THIS MORNING... ...SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 2 PM THIS AFTERNOON TO 3 AM PDT FRIDAY... ...GALE WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM LATE TONIGHT THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING
